title: Indian Lifting Wisdom
summary: NH tours Indian history for lessons in physical culture, from Vedic archery and demanding early yoga, through the Epic-age warrior training and gada swings tied to Hindu gods and Mahabharata heroes, to declines and rebirths ending in 1920s Indian bodybuilding. He argues that male power fantasies and the mind-body 'complete man' produce strong men, and warns India against Western/Bollywood steroid culture.
claims: Every great civilization put physical training at its foundation, as in the line 'no citizen has a right to be an amateur in physical training', attributed to Socrates
In the Vedic age, horse riding and archery were both war preparation and recreation; drawing primitive bows required very strong backs and arms
Ancient yoga was physically demanding and balanced body and mind; weightlifting is a form of weighted yoga with a spiritual side
Western yoga is a corrupted, normie version; lifting must not stoop to normies or it will lose its meaning the same way
Epic-age Indian education included javelin, sword fighting, club swinging and wrestling, taught by the same teachers who taught scripture
Modern people spend about 95% of their time training the mind and 5% the body; the ancient balance was closer to 50/50
The ideal is the complete man, both intellectual and physically fit; modern humans are hyper-specialized for cerebral work
Gada (mace) swings strengthen the upper body and are still used in wrestling gyms; Chris Duffin's Shoulder Rock sells the same idea at ten times the price
Legends tell of kings and soldiers doing a thousand gada swings every morning, then bathing in a lake
Lifting is his meditation; keep spirituality in training, because purely materialistic motives eventually burn out
Hanuman, god of wrestling and devotion, was prayed to by wrestlers and gada swingers, like Greeks praying to Hercules
Mahabharata heroes earned their divinity through feats; male power fantasies like these are what produce strong men in every civilization
Steroided Hollywood actors playing gods are poor role models compared with the mythological originals
He calls France the wimpiest country because it rejects strong role models like Napoleon or de Gaulle
India is westernizing; Bollywood actors are on steroids or TRT and India ranks in the top three for steroid misuse with South Korea and Brazil
The tale of Ekalavya cutting off his thumb for Drona teaches devotion, sacrifice and acceptance of fate; the gods were pre-moral, not perfect
A Krishna statue in Cleveland shows him as very muscular, unlike modern effeminate depictions
When Buddhist influence spread, explosive training declined in favor of pranayama and surya namaskar, mirroring how Christianity softened Europe's knights
Physical culture revived in the Muslim period, declined under British rule, and was reborn in the 1920s with Indian bodybuilders like Ghosh and Sen Gupta
exercises: upper body musculature; direct carryover for soldiers
